newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude closes higher on slim volume.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude closes higher on slim volume.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil prices closed Friday slightly higher while refined products settled lower on profit-taking amid slim volume ahead of the U.S. Labor Day holiday weekend, traders said.
Players also unloaded positions in the September refined products contracts which expired at the end of Friday's session.
September gasoline finished its final day 0.90 cent lower at 62.82 cents a gallon, above its session low of 62.50 cents.
"There was some profit-taking ahead of the weekend coupled with the September expiry," said a trader.
September heating oil ended the day 0.85 cent lower to 62.82 cents a gallon.
"The focus was entirely on the products today," said Fimat USA Futures analyst Rita Beale, adding trading volume in crude was so slim that its rise could not be seen as meaningful.
October crude closed up 10 cents to $22.25 a barrel.

"The cracks were out of line. This just adjusted them and that is what supported crude," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil. Traders sold refined products and bought crude, narrowing the crack spreads which widened after a rally in refined products Thursday, Ritterbusch said.
The October heating oil-to-crude crack spread narrowed to $4.26 a barrel from Thursday's $4.58 while the October gasoline-to-crude spread narrowed to $3.63 from Thursday's $3.86 a barrel.
NYMEX is closed Monday due to the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
Fimat's Beale said October crude may open a few cents higher Tuesday as a beginning of an attempt to close an upside gap on the spot continuation chart that extends to $22.60 a barrel.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, +1 212-859-1761
